title: Joe DiMaggio's Patek Philippe Breguet Dial Reference 130 Chronograph in 18K YG w/ Extract
description: This remains the longest consecutive-game hitting streak in MLB history to this day! Throughout the May 15 to July 16, 1941 streak, he batted .408 with 15 home runs and 55 RBIs. Joltin’ Joe’s career started alongside the “Iron Horse” Lou Gehrig and ended alongside Micky Mantle. He operated at the intersection of two legendary Yankees eras (with Gehrig who played alongside Babe Ruth and was part of the Murderers’ Row 1927 Yankees team) and then with Mantle who of course had the legendary home run duel with his teammate Roger Maris in 1961. From 1943–1945, DiMaggio served in the U.S. Army Air Forces during World War II (which many cite as his prime years). DiMaggio had a lifetime batting average of .325 and accumulated 361 home runs. In 1955, DiMaggio was elected into the National Baseball Hall of Fame. In 1969, Joe DiMaggio was voted the greatest living baseball player. He famously married Marilyn Monroe in 1954 and they had a short marriage, but they rekindled their relationship years later and were reportedly close to marrying again before Monroe passed in 1962. According to the Extract from the Archives, this timepiece was produced in 1947 and was sold on December 12, 1948. The dial features beautiful hand-cut Breguet numerals which are confirmed in the Extract notes. It features the tachymeter scale demarcated for miles on the perimeter of the dial. This example features the spade hand configuration which was popular in the American market during the late 1940s. The watch is powered by the prestigious calibre 13-130 which was featured in many of the most important chronographs from Patek Philippe in this period. The case measures 33mm in diameter, and wears large at 41mm lug-to-lug. The 18k yellow gold case was produced by Emile Vichet, the Geneva master casemaker and features the Poinçon de Maître number 9. (Stainless steel reference 130s were produced by Wenger, Crossier or Dubois.) Emile Vichet produced the gold cases for the legendary Patek Philippe reference

title: Rolex Tropical Double Red Sea-Dweller Reference 1665 Thin Case
description: This Rolex Sea-Dweller reference 1665 features the highly desired and vibrant "Double Red" dial and the rare thin case. The earliest Sea-Dwellers such as this example used cases like on the Rolex Submariner reference 5512, but with a helium escape valve (HEV) added to the left side of the case. The case is lightly polished, but in strong condition overall. The watch measures 40mm in diameter. It previously came from the original owner. The amazing tropical dial has the original tritium lume on the dial and hands. The aluminum bezel insert has faded to a beautiful grey color. The watch features a 1.7 million serial with inside case back dating to circa 1967. These were not assembled by Rolex to be Sea-Dwellers until later. The watch came from the original owner who purchased it new in New Zealand in the early 1970s. The gentleman’s wife was upset about the cost of the watch, but it was already purchased. The gentleman was a roofer and did various forms of manual labor. One day, he was on a roof and he took his watch off and left it on the roof so it would not get damaged while he was working. Unfortunately, he slipped and fell off the roof. He went to the hospital for a few days and when he regained his senses he realized his Rolex was probably still on the roof. He went back about a week later once he had left the hospital and promptly climbed onto the roof to find his watch still sitting there. He joked that spending the week in the sun up on the roof might have helped the dial turn “tropical” brown. The watch does not come with box and papers. Overall, this is an amazing opportunity to get a spectacular and rare Rolex sports watch. We do not know the service history, but it is running well. It recently passed a water resistance test of 5 bar.

title: Heuer USS Whale Carrera Reference 2447S Eggshell Dial
description: This annual watch prize tradition started in 1938 and continues to this day. L.Y. Spear, President of the Electric Boat Company (which became General Dynamics), started the Spear Foundation in 1942 with an endowment to fund the watch prize. The Spear Foundation allowed the shipmate to pick out his own watch from Mallove’s Jewelers in Groton, Connecticut. Brooks wisely selected a Carrera chronograph, but there was a catch. Navy regulations restricted external radioactive sources aboard nuclear-powered boats, so as to ensure accurate monitoring of radiation levels from propulsion systems. This watch had its tritium luminous material removed from dial and hands. An early dial was evidently selected for this purpose. This was possibly done on special order from Heuer, or by the retailer at the time of original sale. Brooks served a distinguished Navy career, including as Commander of the Sturgeon-class nuclear-powered attack submarine USS Whale (SSN-638) from 1975 to 1978, retiring with the rank of Captain. As a civilian, Brooks held important Senate-confirmed positions in government. He was appointed Ambassador to lead negotiation of two strategic arms reduction treaties between the U.S. and Russia, and served as U.S. Undersecretary of Energy for Nuclear Security, responsible for managing the National Nuclear Security Administration (NNSA). The watch is powered by the Valjoux calibre 72. The case is lightly polished but very strong. The dial and hands had the original tritium luminous material removed. The signed crown is original. The watch is fitted on a black leather rally strap from Abel Court with a rare signed vintage “Sun” buckle. The watch does not come with box and papers. It is paired on a folded link bracelet and features a silver dial. The watch is in great shape and appears to be unpolished. The watch does not come with a box or papers. We do not know the service history, but it is running well. It recently passed a water resistance test of 3 bar. This watch is available through J. Press.

title: Rolex 31MM Datejust Reference 6827 in 18k YG w/ Black Dial Unpolished
description: This Rolex Datejust reference 6827 is an incredible watch. It is made of 18k yellow gold and is paired on an 18k yellow gold jubilee Rolex bracelet. The watch dates to circa 1979. The watch measures 31mm in diameter. The case appears to be unpolished. If features a beautiful black dial - it is likely a bit newer, but is extremely attractive. The watch recently passed a water resistance test of 5 bar. It does not come with box or papers. We do not know the service history but it is running well. Vintage 31mm Rolex watches are extremely uncommon and have become very popular by connoisseurs. We believe this is largely due to the fact that @watchabbie wears a 31mm vintage Rolex! Everyone is obsessed with her and that is great! This Watch is available at NET-A-PORTER.

title: 18mm C+B Rolled Link Bracelet in 18k Rose Gold 6 Inches
description: This is a remarkable vintage bracelet in 14k rose gold. It is produced by C+B but does not feature the maker’s initials. C+B bracelets were sold on timepieces at Cartier and Tiffany & Co. New York. This example is a sophisticated rolled-link style that is approximately 6 inches in length. The straight end links are approximately 18mm wide. The bracelet measures 40 grams. This would look outstanding on a rose gold dress watch from Cartier, Patek Philippe, Audemars Piguet, or any manufacturer from the mid-century. For those looking to upgrade their rose gold timepiece, this is a fantastic pairing.
